newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-PISTONS SIGN BRIAN WILLIAMS TO SEVEN-YEAR CONTRACT.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-PISTONS SIGN BRIAN WILLIAMS TO SEVEN-YEAR CONTRACT.

text.p: Free-agent forward-center Brian Williams, who parlayed a holdout into an NBA championship with the Chicago Bulls, signed a seven-year contract with the rival Detroit Pistons Saturday.
Financial terms were not disclosed, although a team spokesman said the deal includes an option that would allow Williams to again become a free agent in three years.
Last year, Williams rejected a seven-year, $35 million offer from Seattle and a four-year, $16 million offer from the Los Angeles Clippers.
After holding out and nursing an injury for nearly the entire season, the 6-11 (2.11 metres) Williams signed a pro-rated minimum contract with the Bulls in April.
As the playoffs progressed, he became more of an integral part of the team and averaged 6.8 points in Chicago's six-game victory over the Utah Jazz in the NBA Finals.

The 27-year-old Williams fills a gaping hole for the Pistons, who have won 100 games and reached the playoffs each of the last two years without a legitimate center. They have used a small lineup, often with forwards Theo Ratliff, Rick Mahorn and Don Reid manning the middle.

Salary cap room was created for Williams when the Pistons traded forward Otis Thorpe, who makes $5.8 million next season, to the Vancouver Grizzlies last week for a future first-round pick. Also, the salary cap expanded $2.5 million for all teams Friday.

The enigmatic Williams joins the fifth team of his six-year career. He was the 10th overall pick of the Orlando Magic in 1991 and was dealt to the Denver Nuggets two years later after admittedly attempting suicide.

Williams averaged eight points and 5.3 rebounds per game in two seasons with the Nuggets before he was traded to the Clippers, where he started for the first time and flourished. He averaged career highs of 15.8 points and 7.6 rebounds in 1995-96 and opted out of his contract, becoming a free agent.

But Williams never got the lucrative deal he was seeking. He ended up without a team and suffered a knee injury that caused him to fail a physical in January, when the Dallas Mavericks were interested in signing him. He later turned down a $1 million offer from Utah, instead taking $27,000 from Chicago.
In nine games, Williams averaged seven points and 3.7 rebounds with the Bulls. In the playoffs, he averaged 6.1 points and 3.7 rebounds, providing a boost as starter Dennis Rodman struggled.
In addition to trading Thorpe, the Pistons re-signed free-agent guards Joe Dumars and Lindsey Hunter. Reid, Mahorn and forward Terry Mills remain unsigned.
